plate_findings.evidence: Coronary artery stiffness, left coronary artery segmental stenosis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Coronary CTA in a child with sitosterolemia shows coronary artery stiffness and segmental stenosis, consistent with premature atherosclerosis. B: Abdominal CTA in a child with sitosterolemia and atherosclerosis shows aortic wall thickening/dilation and proximal renal artery narrowing; disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused case report title and captioned vascular manifestations. C: Abdominal CTA in a child with sitosterolemia and atherosclerosis shows thickened/dilated aorta with visceral arterial narrowing; attribution supported by case report context and panel-specific caption. D: Three-dimensional CTA reconstruction in a child with sitosterolemia and atherosclerosis shows abdominal aortic and branch vessel abnormalities; attribution supported by disease-focused case report and panel-specific caption.

in_text_mentions: Dynamic electrocardiogram (ECG) indicated frequent ventricular premature beats, paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, and occasional ventricular premature beats. Coronary CTA showed thickening of the aortic wall, stiffness of the coronary arteries, and changes in left and right arteries segmental stenoses (Figure 2A).

Abdominal computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed a thickened abdominal aortic wall, unevenly dilated, bilateral proximal renal artery, celiac trunk, and narrowing of the superior mesenteric artery (Figures 2B–D).
